t: Dataset Diff Engine: a plain-language overview
title: Dataset Diff Engine: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Dataset Diff Engine does and why archives need it. A dataset diff engine compares two versions of a whole dataset and tells you exactly what changed: which records were added, which were deleted, and which were modified. It matches records by their keys across versions, so renames and reorderings do not fool it. Big data in, precise changelog out.
demo:
# Dataset Diff Engine - runnable demo (JAH-ATK182-000001)
import hashlib, json
RANK = 1
SIG = False
OLD, NEW = ([{'id': 'r1', 'v': 1}, {'id': 'r2', 'v': 1}, {'id': 'r3', 'v': 1}], [{'id': 'r1', 'v': 1}, {'id': 'r2', 'v': 2}, {'id': 'r4', 'v': 1}])
def h(r): return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
old, new = {r["id"]: r for r in OLD}, {r["id"]: r for r in NEW}
added = [k for k in new if k not in old]
deleted = [k for k in old if k not in new]
modified = [k for k in old if k in new and h(old[k]) != h(new[k])]
print("added:", added, "| deleted:", deleted, "| modified:", modified)
for k in modified:
    diffs = [f for f in set(old[k]) | set(new[k]) if old[k].get(f) != new[k].get(f)]
    print("  %s changed fields: %s" % (k, diffs))
if RANK >= 2:
    print("unchanged:", len(old) - len(deleted) - len(modified), "/", len(old))
if RANK >= 3:
    print("snapshot hashes: old=%s new=%s" % (h(sorted(old)), h(sorted(new))))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-DIF-" + "JAH-ATK182-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK182-000001", "OK")

t: How the Dataset Diff Engine works
title: How the Dataset Diff Engine works
description: Overview: what the Dataset Diff Engine does and why archives need it. Real diff engines index both snapshots by primary key, then classify every key as added (new key), deleted (missing key), unchanged (identical hash), or modified (same key, different hash). Modified records get field-level diffs, large diffs stream in chunks to bound memory, and hash chaining (Merkle-style) lets the engine skip identical partitions quickly. The output is a structured changelog with counts and per-record change details.

t: How the Dataset Diff Engine works: the deep tour
title: How the Dataset Diff Engine works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Dataset Diff Engine does and why archives need it. Real diff engines index both snapshots by primary key, then classify every key as added (new key), deleted (missing key), unchanged (identical hash), or modified (same key, different hash). Modified records get field-level diffs, large diffs stream in chunks to bound memory, and hash chaining (Merkle-style) lets the engine skip identical partitions quickly. The output is a structured changelog with counts and per-record change details. Advanced engines handle key changes (a record re-keyed is matched by fuzzy similarity, not counted as delete+add), schema evolution between versions, and ordered datasets where position matters. Quality is measured by diff correctness on synthetic version pairs with known edits. The limits are keyless datasets, where matching is heuristic, and semantic changes invisible to hashing — those need content-aware comparison layered on top, and the engine reports its matching confidence per record.

title: The Dataset Diff Engine at archive scale
description: Production: how the Dataset Diff Engine runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real diff engines index both snapshots by primary key, then classify every key as added (new key), deleted (missing key), unchanged (identical hash), or modified (same key, different hash). Modified records get field-level diffs, large diffs stream in chunks to bound memory, and hash chaining (Merkle-style) lets the engine skip identical partitions quickly. The output is a structured changelog with counts and per-record change details. Advanced engines handle key changes (a record re-keyed is matched by fuzzy similarity, not counted as delete+add), schema evolution between versions, and ordered datasets where position matters. Quality is measured by diff correctness on synthetic version pairs with known edits. The limits are keyless datasets, where matching is heuristic, and semantic changes invisible to hashing — those need content-aware comparison layered on top, and the engine reports its matching confidence per record.
